locus-pro:
Locus Pro: pay-per-use APIs billed to one credit balance.

For repeatable Workflows, load the registered locus-workflows skill when available; otherwise call get_locus_guide. Call web_research for grounded answers, web_extract for exact URLs, router_web_search for sources, or commerce_search for products. Otherwise use search_apis(query), then execute(slug, args) with its returned schema. For enabled:false, call request_tool_access and send its approval_url to the human. describe_api(slug) refreshes contracts. Use estimate_cost only for an exact quote or hard ceiling. Read balances with get_balance().

Calls are live and billed; charges appear in structuredContent and _meta. RETRIES: pass "idempotency_key" to execute (or _meta "locus/idempotencyKey" on any burn tool) — the same key never double-charges. Without one, retries deduplicate best-effort; intentional repeats need a fresh key. Replays carry idempotent_replay:true and no new charge. For quotes, reuse approval_token and idempotency_key unchanged; price movement returns MCP_APPROVAL_REAPPROVAL_REQUIRED before dispatch. Use ?compact=1 for compact text.

AUTH: interactive clients use discovered OAuth and consent. Service credentials include tenant keys and scoped agent credentials; end-user credentials remain user-bound. Failures return isError:true with an actionable hint.
apollo: This server provides access to Apollo.io APIs for lead generation, enrichment, and sales engagement. Use the available tools to search contacts, companies, manage opportunities, sequences, and more. Credit-consuming tool responses may include an mcp_credits block (estimated cost, actual spend, and credit balance); when present, always surface it to the user unprompted — the estimated cost before further spends (including expected/max ranges for waterfall add-ons) and, once a spend settles, the credits used and the new balance. Authentication is required via OAuth 2.0. OAuth server metadata is available at https://mcp.apollo.io/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server A tool response may include an apollo_plan_limit block. When it does, the user has hit an Apollo plan or credit limit, and that block's `message` is the complete answer: relay it verbatim as your entire reply, including its link exactly as given. Do not summarise or rewrite it, do not suggest alternatives or other tools to try, do not add any other link, and do not end with a question.
firecrawl: Firecrawl provides web search, page retrieval, site URL discovery, multi-page collection, structured page data, monitoring, and multi-source research that returns structured data. Match the requested operation to the tool boundary: firecrawl_scrape retrieves one supplied page and can return JSON matching a supplied schema, firecrawl_map enumerates URLs under a site without retrieving their content, and firecrawl_agent runs multi-source research and returns structured data when the URLs are not known or the answer spans several sites (an entity plus its fields, a list, a dataset); its result is read with firecrawl_agent_status. Authenticated firecrawl_search returns web results together with matching Alexandria providers in data.tools. Alexandria is Firecrawl's catalogue of data providers and workflows across companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more; providers return typed, sourced records through published contracts. A matching provider can return the same fields across several entities, provenance, exact figures or timestamps, or a large set of records through firecrawl_scrape with its published contract. If web results already answer the question, use them. For the same fields across multiple pages, firecrawl_find_tools offers free provider discovery. Use firecrawl_find_tools to read a contract that was not returned in full or to browse the catalogue by category. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. If no provider fits, continue with web search or firecrawl_agent. For biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature, the firecrawl_research_* tools search a paper index of abstracts and full text; firecrawl_search with categories: ["research"] is a website filter over ordinary web results and reaches different sources. For a programming question (code behaviour, a library or framework, an API contract, an error message, or a known bug), firecrawl_developer_search (or firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"]) searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and code documentation. firecrawl_search with sources: [{type: "alexandria"}] returns compact tool summaries in data.tools; toolDetail: "full" includes contracts, firecrawl_find_tools starts with categories, lists providers, then compact tools, and expands the selected full contract, and firecrawl_scrape with alexandria: [{provider, capability, options}] executes up to ten capabilities and returns their results. Alexandria access needs an API key on a team with it enabled. Provide only the required inputs and account for stated network or external side effects.
